The national dataset for [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]] outlines the demographic and diagnostic profiles of patients receiving [[bmsl|Biologiske og målrettede syntetiske lægemidler]] (BMSL) across Denmark [^src1]. Because the data represents a single snapshot from the 2024 report, no longitudinal trends can be established [^src1].

In terms of patient volume, adults heavily outnumber children in BMSL treatment, with 11,464 adult patients compared to 407 pediatric patients [^src1]. The diagnostic distribution reveals a clear divergence between the two age groups. Among children, Crohn's disease (DK50*) is the leading diagnosis, accounting for 69% (282 patients) of the pediatric cohort, while ulcerative colitis (DK51*) represents 31% (125 patients) [^src1]. Conversely, adults show a more balanced but still Crohn's-dominant profile, with 61% (6,960 patients) diagnosed with Crohn's disease and 39% (4,444 patients) with ulcerative colitis [^src1]. Rare conditions such as primary sclerosing cholangitis (DK830F) and short bowel syndrome (DK912B) act as outliers, recorded with just 40 and 20 cases respectively, and their specific age breakdowns are not detailed in this table [^src1].

Gender distribution also varies by age. The pediatric group skews male, with 58% (235 patients) being male and 42% (172 patients) female [^src1]. In contrast, the adult population is evenly split, with exactly 50% (5,755 patients) female and 50% (5,709 patients) male [^src1]. 

Age statistics highlight the expected boundaries of the cohorts: the pediatric average age is 14 years (range 0-18), with a median of 15 years [^src1]. The adult cohort has an average age of 43 years (range 17-97) and a median of 41 years [^src1].

Summary: Tabellen sammenligner demografiske og diagnostiske karakteristika for børn og voksne patienter i behandling med BMSL på nationalt plan, hvor Crohns sygdom dominerer hos børn og ulcerøs colitis er mere udbredt hos voksne.
